summary: Never-built observation tower planned for a campground on Loudoun Heights near Harpers Ferry, WV; footings and stairs remain. The register's 'removed' note conflicts.

facts.status_note: Never built. The Appalachian Trail lookout page says footings and bottom stairs remain; its 2024 visit section describes the overgrown side trail and the three-minute walk.

access.note: Less than 0.1 mile off the Appalachian Trail. The sources read mention no closure or permit. Ownership of the footings is not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: Less than 0.1 mile off the Appalachian Trail with about a 20-foot gain. The old side trail is mostly overgrown; about a three-minute walk per a 2024 visit, and easy to miss.

events.note: Registered October 5, 2009, nominated by Bill Spach. Register describes the tower as removed; other sources say it was never built.

corrections.why: Never built. The Appalachian Trail lookout page and the county table both say never built, and footings and bottom stairs remain per the trail page. 'Ruins' is the vocabulary value for footings or remains only.
No tower was built. The county table lists an observation tower that was never built; no standing or former structure exists to classify. Editor to confirm the kind value.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower has been removed and the site appears to have once been enclosed by a chain-link fence. The Appalachian Trail lookout page and the county table say it was never built. The story follows the trail page and the county table, which agree, and says the register disagrees.

notes_for_editor: The brief's 'gone' status is wrong on the best evidence: two sources say never built, and the register's removal line is the outlier. Bill Spach is both the register's nominator and the person quoted on the trail page, so the conflict is within one person's accounts; asking him directly would settle it. The NPS page in the cache describes stone blockhouse foundations on the summit (1861). It is not confirmed that these are the same stonework as the footings on the trail page, so the story only raises the question. An earlier fetch of the same NPS URL returned an intro with more text (park acreage, trail) that the cache no longer returns; the checker reads the current cache, so only that text is quoted. Ownership of the footings is not confirmed. Clio's page returned no text in the fetch, so it is not used. Wikipedia's Loudoun Heights (Mountain) page had no tower mention. Two searches and about five page reads.
